name: British Industrial Revolution
what: The shift in Britain to machine production powered by water and then coal-fired steam, centred on Lancashire cotton.

name: Britain's cheap-coal economy
what: Coalfields close to towns and water transport made British coal among the cheapest energy in the world.

name: North-west Europe's high-wage economy
what: London and Amsterdam labourers earned more silver and more food per day than workers elsewhere in Europe or Asia.

name: Atlantic trade boom
what: The growth of slave-grown sugar, tobacco and cotton trades and of Atlantic markets for British manufactures.

name: Industrious revolution
what: Households in north-west Europe worked more days and more members for the market, to buy new goods.

name: Little Divergence: the North Sea economies pull ahead
what: England and the Low Countries kept the income gains of the late Middle Ages while Italy and Spain fell back.

name: Great Divergence
what: Western Europe and its offshoots grew rich in sustained fashion while China and India stagnated or fell back.

name: Mechanisation of cotton spinning
what: The spinning jenny, water frame and mule cut the labour needed to spin a pound of cotton by orders of magnitude.

name: Calico Acts
what: Parliament banned imports and then the wearing of most printed Indian cottons, sheltering a home industry.

name: Britain's pool of skilled mechanics
what: Clockmakers, millwrights, instrument makers and smiths able to build, fix and improve machines.

name: Survival of the richest in England
what: Gregory Clark's finding from wills that richer English testators left more surviving children than poorer ones.

name: France in the American War of Independence
what: French intervention against Britain, financed largely by loans rather than taxes.

name: Eden Treaty
what: The Anglo-French commercial treaty that cut tariffs and let British textiles into France.

name: French royal bankruptcy crisis
what: From Calonne's admission of the deficit in August 1786 to the treasury's suspension of payments on 16 August 1788.

name: Assembly of Notables of 1787
what: The handpicked elite that refused to approve Calonne's tax reforms without wider consent.

name: Drought of spring and summer 1788 in France
what: A dry, hot spring and early summer that stunted grain across northern France.

name: Hailstorm of 13 July 1788
what: A line of hailstorms that flattened crops in a band across northern France on the eve of harvest.

name: French harvest failure of 1788
what: A poor grain harvest that drove bread prices up through the winter of 1788-89.

name: Hard winter of 1788-89
what: A severe winter that froze rivers and mills and halted work around Paris.

name: Paris bread price peak of 1789
what: The four-pound loaf in Paris rose from about 9 sous in mid-1788 to 14.5 sous, its level on 14 July 1789.

name: Great Fear
what: The rural panic of late July and early August 1789, when rumours of brigands set villages arming and attacking chateaux.

name: Night of 4 August 1789
what: The National Assembly session that voted to abolish feudal privileges.

name: Assignat inflation
what: Paper money backed by confiscated church land, printed to cover deficits until it lost almost all its value.

name: European harvest failure of 1816
what: Cold and rain ruined grain, potatoes and wine across western and central Europe.

name: Subsistence crisis of 1816-17
what: Post's 'last great subsistence crisis in the Western world': high grain prices, begging, disease and excess deaths.

name: Yunnan famine of 1815-17
what: Cold summers wrecked rice harvests in the south-western Chinese province of Yunnan.

name: Emigration wave of 1816-17
what: Tens of thousands of south-west Germans and Swiss left via the Rhine for America and Russia.

name: New England summer frosts of 1816
what: June, July and August frosts that killed crops in Vermont, New Hampshire and Maine.

name: Irish population growth on the potato
what: Ireland grew to about 8.2 million people by the 1841 census, a third of them eating little but potatoes.

name: Potato blight reaches Ireland
what: Phytophthora infestans, a water mould from the Americas, rotted much of the potato crop from September 1845.

name: Irish public works relief
what: Road and drainage schemes that paid the starving for labour; employment peaked at over 700,000 in March 1847.

name: Soup kitchens of 1847
what: Under the Temporary Relief Act, kitchens fed about three million people a day at their peak in mid-1847.

name: Poor Law Extension Act and Gregory clause
what: Shifted relief onto Irish poor rates and denied it to anyone holding more than a quarter acre of land.

name: Irish grain and livestock exports during the famine
what: Oats, wheat and cattle continued to leave Irish ports in 1845-47 while maize was imported.

name: Famine fever
what: Typhus, relapsing fever and dysentery that killed more famine victims than starvation itself.

name: Famine clearances
what: Landlords evicted tenants who could not pay rent or poor rates, most heavily in Clare and the west.

name: Lytton's famine relief policy
what: Viceroy Lytton's government cut relief, required heavy labour for it, and fixed the 'Temple wage' ration.

name: Indian grain exports during the 1876-78 famine
what: Grain kept moving to ports and abroad by rail and ship while the Deccan starved.

name: Decline of the Qing granary system
what: The ever-normal granaries that had blunted eighteenth-century famines were run down by fiscal strain and rebellion.

name: Indian Famine Commission and Famine Codes
what: The 1880 Famine Commission report and the provincial Famine Codes that followed it set rules for relief.

name: Franco-Russian Alliance
what: The military alliance that faced Germany with a two-front war.

name: Austro-Hungarian ultimatum to Serbia
what: The 48-hour ultimatum of 23 July 1914, written to be refused.

name: Russian general mobilisation
what: Ordered on 30 July 1914 after pre-mobilisation measures begun on 25-26 July.

name: German invasion of Belgium
what: The Schlieffen-Moltke plan sent German armies through Belgium on 4 August 1914, bringing Britain in.

name: Treaty of Versailles
what: The peace with Germany, signed 28 June 1919, with war-guilt and reparations clauses.

name: Reparations and inter-Allied war debts
what: German reparations and Allied debts to the United States that tied interwar finance in knots.

name: Interwar gold standard restored
what: Britain returned to gold at the pre-war parity in April 1925; most of the world was back on gold by 1928.

name: Federal Reserve tightening of 1928-29
what: The Fed raised rates to curb stock speculation, pulling gold to the US and squeezing other countries.

name: Wall Street Crash
what: The New York stock market collapse of late October 1929.

name: Collapse of American consumer spending in 1930
what: US consumption, above all of cars and other durables, fell sharply in 1930.

name: American banking panics of 1930-33
what: Four waves of bank runs in which about 9,000 American banks failed.

name: Great Depression
what: The worldwide slump in which US output fell by about a quarter and industrial production by nearly half between 1929 and 1933.

name: Smoot-Hawley Tariff
what: The US tariff of June 1930 that raised duties on thousands of imports and drew retaliation.

name: Creditanstalt collapse
what: Austria's largest bank failed in May 1931, setting off runs across central Europe.

name: German banking crisis of 1931
what: The Danatbank failure in July 1931 and the bank holiday that followed.

name: Britain leaves the gold standard
what: Sterling floated on 21 September 1931 after a run on the pound.

name: Nazi seizure of power
what: Hitler became chancellor on 30 January 1933 after the Nazi vote rose from 2.6 to 37.3 percent in four years.

name: Second World War
what: The war that began with the German invasion of Poland in September 1939 and ended in August-September 1945.

name: Kristallnacht
what: The pogrom of 9-10 November 1938 across Germany and Austria.

name: Madagascar Plan
what: The 1940 scheme to deport Europe's Jews to Madagascar, dropped when Britain could not be defeated at sea.

name: Operation Barbarossa
what: The German invasion of the Soviet Union on 22 June 1941.

name: Hunger Plan
what: German planners intended to divert Soviet grain to Germany and let tens of millions starve.

name: Mass shootings by the Einsatzgruppen
what: SS task forces, police battalions and local auxiliaries shot Jews in the occupied Soviet Union, including 33,771 at Babi Yar in two days.

name: Wannsee Conference
what: The meeting of 20 January 1942 where Heydrich coordinated ministries for the murder of Europe's Jews.

name: Operation Reinhard death camps
what: Belzec, Sobibor and Treblinka, where about 1.7 million Jews were gassed.

name: The Holocaust
what: The murder of about six million European Jews by Nazi Germany and its collaborators.

name: Yalta Conference
what: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin met in February 1945 to settle postwar Europe and the war with Japan.

name: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
what: The United States destroyed two Japanese cities with atomic bombs on 6 and 9 August 1945.

name: Soviet takeover of eastern Europe
what: Communist regimes imposed in Poland, Romania, Bulgaria, Hungary and, in February 1948, Czechoslovakia.

name: Long Telegram
what: George Kennan's analysis of Soviet conduct, cabled from Moscow on 22 February 1946.

name: Truman Doctrine
what: Truman asked Congress for aid to Greece and Turkey and pledged support to free peoples on 12 March 1947.

name: Marshall Plan
what: About $13 billion of American aid to western Europe, announced June 1947 and paid 1948-52.

name: Berlin Blockade
what: Stalin cut land access to West Berlin from June 1948 to May 1949; the West supplied it by air.

name: Cold War
what: The global rivalry between the United States and the Soviet Union and their allies.

name: Chinese Communist victory
what: Mao proclaimed the People's Republic on 1 October 1949.

name: Korean War
what: North Korea's invasion of the South in June 1950, with Stalin's approval, and the war that followed.

name: Soviet war in Afghanistan
what: The Soviet intervention of December 1979 and nine-year war.

name: Oil price collapse of 1986
what: Saudi Arabia raised output and the oil price roughly halved, cutting Soviet hard-currency earnings.

name: Perestroika economic reforms
what: The Law on State Enterprise (1987), legal cooperatives (1988) and failed attempts to free prices.

name: Glasnost and democratisation
what: Open criticism in the press and contested elections to the Congress of People's Deputies in March 1989.

name: Soviet budget and supply crisis
what: Deficits financed by printing money emptied shops and fed rationing and strikes.

name: Revolutions of 1989
what: Communist regimes in eastern Europe fell, and the Berlin Wall opened on 9 November 1989.

name: Nationalist mobilisation in the Soviet republics
what: Mass movements in the Baltic, the Caucasus and Ukraine demanding sovereignty and then independence.

name: August coup
what: Hardliners tried to seize power on 19-21 August 1991 and failed against Yeltsin and the Moscow crowds.

name: Ukrainian independence referendum
what: On 1 December 1991 over 90 percent of Ukrainian voters backed independence.

name: Belovezha Accords
what: Russia, Ukraine and Belarus declared on 8 December 1991 that the USSR had ceased to exist.

name: Government of India Act 1935
what: Gave elected Indian ministries power in the provinces and proposed an all-India federation.

name: Lahore Resolution
what: The Muslim League demand of 23 March 1940 for independent states in the Muslim-majority north-west and east.

name: Quit India movement
what: Congress demanded immediate British withdrawal in August 1942; its leaders were jailed for most of the war.

name: Indian elections of 1945-46
what: The Muslim League won nearly all Muslim seats, Congress most general seats.

name: Cabinet Mission Plan
what: The British plan of May 1946 for a loose three-tier federation keeping India united.

name: Direct Action Day and the Great Calcutta Killings
what: The Muslim League protest of 16 August 1946 that became days of killing in Calcutta, followed by Noakhali and Bihar.

name: Hindu demand to partition Bengal
what: Bengal Hindu leaders campaigned in 1947 for a separate West Bengal inside India.

name: Mountbatten Plan
what: Announced 3 June 1947: partition of India, of Punjab and of Bengal, with transfer of power brought forward to 15 August 1947.

name: Partition of India
what: British India divided into the Dominions of India and Pakistan on 14-15 August 1947.

name: Radcliffe boundary awards
what: The Punjab and Bengal boundaries, published on 17 August 1947, two days after independence.

name: Punjab partition violence
what: Massacres of Muslims, Hindus and Sikhs in Punjab from March 1947, peaking in August-September.

name: First Kashmir War
what: Tribal raiders and then the Indian and Pakistani armies fought over Jammu and Kashmir.

name: Decolonisation of Asia and Africa
what: Dozens of new states in thirty years as the British, French, Dutch, Belgian and Portuguese empires ended.

name: Antisemitism
what: Hostility to Jews, religious and, from the nineteenth century, racial.
